key_features.classic_presentation: IBS presents with chronic/recurrent abdominal pain associated with bowel habit changes (diarrhea, constipation, or alternating). Pain relieved by defecation. Bloating common. NO red flags (no blood, weight loss, fever, nocturnal symptoms). Diagnosis of exclusion.
key_features.typical_demographics: 10-15% of population. Female predominance (2:1). Peak onset 20-40 years. Associated with stress, anxiety.
key_features.pathophysiology_brief: Functional disorder (no structural abnormality). Visceral hypersensitivity and altered gut motility.

diagnostic_questions.context: IBS is chronic (>6 months). New acute symptoms suggest other diagnosis.
Pain relief with defecation is a Rome IV criterion for IBS.
RED FLAGS rule OUT IBS. IBS doesn't cause: bleeding, weight loss, fever, nocturnal symptoms.
Pain is usually mild-moderate, not severe.

differential_diagnosis.key_difference: Blood in stool, weight loss, fever, inflammation on testing
Diarrhea after gluten, weight loss, nutrient deficiencies

red_flags.action: Need colonoscopy to rule out malignancy

red_flags.finding: ANY alarm symptoms (blood, weight loss, fever, anemia)
red_flags.action: Not IBS - needs workup for organic disease

typical_management: Dietary modifications (low FODMAP), fiber, antispasmodics, loperamide for diarrhea. Stress management, CBT. Symptom-directed therapy.
disposition: Outpatient management. Referral to GI if not responding to initial therapy.
patient_education: IBS is a functional bowel disorder causing chronic symptoms without structural damage. While not dangerous, it can be uncomfortable. Treatment focuses on symptom management and lifestyle changes.
